forks.decision: FeatureBench runs through our runner with the agent inside the task container and the pinned upstream fb eval grader in a fresh container
One evolutionary loop mutates code and text; a candidate is a commit
The loop engine is GEPA optimize_anything with repeat runs on frontier candidates
The loop may mutate all of src and prompts except evaluator paths; winners land as human-reviewed draft PRs
The judge labels per-task applicability and critiques each rollout for reflection only; grader correctness is the only objective
The Phase 4 power gate is retired; every paid run requires an explicit dollar ceiling

contradictions: Approach step 5 and AC-11 say prompt mutations are allowed and the applier 'updates the byte lock mechanically', but AC-11 rejects diffs to #[cfg(test)] spans. The byte lock (src/mcp/mod.rs:771, inside `mod tests` at :456) is more than a length: it asserts starts_with/ends_with/contains on specific prompt phrases. cwd_guidance_spans_present (:2292) also checks the #[cfg(test)] CWD_PATHS_SPAN const (:81). Only the 1966 byte count can be updated mechanically. A prompts/** mutation that touches any asserted phrase fails `cargo test` and can never be repaired, so F-4's 'all of prompts' is not actually available. The same rule freezes any src/** behavior that an in-source unit test asserts.

F-4 and Approach step 5 frame mutation as an allowlist (src/** and prompts/** minus evaluator paths), but AC-11 is a denylist: benchmark/**, tests/**, .github/**, the Cargo.toml version line, and #[cfg(test)] spans. Under AC-11 a diff to the rest of Cargo.toml, justfile, npm/, CLAUDE.md, or scripts/ (including scripts/regen-agents-md.sh, which the applier itself runs, and scripts/verify.py) is admissible, which contradicts the src+prompts scope. Some of those are evaluator paths that the denylist misses.

The minor decision says 'the judge model is pinned and recorded in the run key', but the run key bound in entity_referent_bindings (model id, agent CLI version, dataset revision, effort, timeout, task, arm, repetition) has no judge model. AC-8 keys the label cache on a separate tuple (task, dataset revision, judge model, prompt hash) while also saying 'for its run key'.
orphaned_decisions: F-6 first half ('The Phase 4 power gate is retired'): only Approach step 1 and the crust delta mention marking PHASE4_PLAN.md superseded. No Acceptance criterion or test contract enforces or observes the retirement. AC-7 covers only the dollar-ceiling half.
unsupported_assumptions: That a GEPA optimize_anything candidate can represent and mutate an arbitrary whole-src/** plus prompts/** change. F-2, F-3, AC-11 and evolve.materialize all depend on this, yet the spec defers it to an Open Question [TBD] (unified diff as a text component vs a custom coding-agent proposer) and cites only the optimize_anything blog post.

That --max-usd can be 'summed from native cost'. Codex rows have no native cost: parse.py:337-341 computes total_cost_usd from pricing.yaml via compute_cost_breakdown, and the wiki records 33.7% pricing drift. The 'next cell's estimate' in AC-7 also has no stated source.

That the pinned fb eval can correctly grade a patch extracted by our own replayed Level 1 container setup. AC-3 preflight grades only the dataset's gold, empty, and tampered patches. It never round-trips a patch produced by our prepare_container + `git diff --cached`, so nothing shows our base state matches the state fb eval applies patches against.

That the run key identifies a stock baseline. For the in-house tasks (gin_edit_render_context, rg_*, gin_servehttp_flow), the key has only the task name: no hash of the task prompt, ground_truth, test_command, or fixture commit. Editing a task in benchmark/tasks/*.py would silently reuse stale 'frozen' baselines (G-5, AC-6, AC-13).
acceptance_gaps: G-4 (research model reasons over raw result JSONL): AC-5 proves only that a sidecar exists. AC-10's test contract (test_score_ignores_judge) proves only that the score ignores critiques. No AC or test asserts that the reflection or research model's input actually contains the untruncated row and trajectory content.

G-6 (judge decides where structural tools apply): AC-8 and AC-9 produce and cache labels and gate them on calibration. No AC requires a consumer of the labels, such as slicing or reporting results by applicability or routing them into reflection, so the 'decides where' outcome is never observed.
F-5 'critiques each rollout': no AC requires judge.critique to run for each rollout. AC-9 and AC-10 refer to critiques, but nothing makes the system produce one per rollout.

F-3: AC-13's test contract (test_paid_tier_reuses_baselines) tests baseline reuse only. No test covers the 'repeat runs on frontier candidates' requirement, and no AC or test ties the engine to GEPA optimize_anything.

F-6 'every paid run requires an explicit dollar ceiling': AC-7 and its test cover only run.py cells. evolve.main takes --max-usd in the sketch, but no AC requires the optimizer run to refuse to start without it. No AC counts the judge calls and GEPA reflection-LM spend against the ceiling, and both are paid.

F-4 'the cascade is the backstop': AC-12 runs tests/mcp_v2 only when src/edit/** changed. tests/mcp_v2 also guards fork-law surfaces outside src/edit, such as test_retired_tools.py and cwd anchoring/routing. A src/mcp/** mutation could re-register a retired tool or weaken cwd handling and still pass the cascade. The cascade is also not the CI gate (`just check`).

G-3 (and the goal's 'grow the benchmark'): the cherry-picks are three tasks already registered in benchmark/tasks/__init__.py (rg_search_dispatch, rg_trait_implementors, gin_servehttp_flow), and gin_edit_render_context already exists too. AC-4 only re-lists existing tasks in a panel. External cherry-picks were moved to an [AGENT-INTRODUCED] non-goal, so no AC shows the benchmark grows beyond FeatureBench.
